correctness.rationale: Explicit transfer branches give variation contraction and a uniformly bounded Poisson solution for all centered BV observables. Green--Kubo equals ||h||²−||P h||², also a finite-branch conditional variance. Zero variance forces h(x)=H(ax)=H(bx); coprime-reduced Fourier descent proves H constant for all distinct integer slopes. The stationary reversed process has a bounded martingale approximation, mixing ensures its quadratic variation converges, and the bounded-increment martingale CLT proves the annealed normal law. Uniform resolvent differentiability at zero and cancellation of h-prime terms give exactly ||ψ∘T_a−ψ∘T_b||²; Fourier rigidity makes it strictly positive for nonconstant ψ. Exact rational Fourier tests include resonant powers and divisible slopes; they are supplemental, not proof.

originality.rationale: Exact predecessor comparison: Aimino--Nicol--Vaienti Proposition 3.4 already supplies the general coboundary obstruction and Theorem 3.5 the CLT; Example 7.3 explicitly covers random integer multipliers. Suzuki 2023 supplies random beta transformations and Bernoulli-density response. Dragičević--Hafouta supplies broad differentiability of quenched asymptotic variances. None of those inspected statements presents the all-distinct-slope Fourier-rigidity exclusion together with the evaluated one-sided annealed noise coefficient, or the illustrative arithmetic resonance. The mathematical-source comparisons did not identify an equivalent result. Residual literature priority risk remains because negative searches never certify global absence.
residual_risks: Potential earlier equivalent theorem formulated as common-coboundary rigidity or a rare-noise susceptibility identity but not surfaced by searches; absence from indexes is not proof of publication priority.
The broad 2024 variance-differentiability work was inspected for its relevant theorems rather than read line-for-line; a differently formulated special example elsewhere could alter priority.

The arithmetic all-slope rigidity is elementary once the general coboundary criterion is known; novelty is claimed for the combined strict nondegeneracy and exact first-order noise-onset law, not for general martingale limit theory.

value.rationale: Deterministic expanding circle maps possess infinitely many nonconstant zero-variance coboundaries, so strict nondegeneracy under stochastic switching is a meaningful structural question, not an automatic feature of a central limit theorem. The universal two-slope result covers even multiplicatively dependent integer maps and all BV observables. The exact rare-switch derivative identifies a natural measurable variance susceptibility for arbitrary deterministic coboundaries, with the geometric mismatch energy as coefficient and an exact arithmetic-resonant Fourier test. This supplies a quantitative boundary law useful for studying stability of fluctuations; finite computations alone are not offered as value.
